context.situation: I am chief executive of a regional media group. Classified advertising is roughly 40% of our revenue and funds the newsroom. A team has proposed we launch a free online classifieds platform. It would be loss-making for at least three years and would cannibalise our highest-margin product. Our print circulation is flat, not declining. Two small online competitors exist but they have no revenue and their listings are thin. My board will not accept a proposal that reduces this year's earnings for a speculative position, and honestly I find the case unproven.
context.whatMatters: Protecting the earnings that fund the newsroom.
context.stakeholders: Board, shareholders, newsroom staff, advertisers, readers.
context.uncertainties: Whether online classifieds will actually displace print.

evidence.text: Classified advertising is approximately 40% of revenue.
Print circulation is flat rather than declining.
Two online competitors exist with thin listings and no revenue.
The proposed platform would be loss-making for at least three years.
The board will not approve a reduction in this year's earnings.
Younger readers are not entering the print subscriber base.
Our sales team reports advertisers are satisfied.
